offence_severity: Death (Section 302 IPC) - Minimum: Life imprisonment, Maximum: Death
physical_harm: The appellant strangulated his wife with a 'saria', causing her death
number_of_offences: Charged under Section 302 IPC; upheld under Section 302 IPC, modified to Section 304 Part II
premeditation_planning: The court found no premeditation, the act was committed in a heat of passion
key_evidence_accepted: The Supreme Court accepted the testimony of PW-7, the son of the accused and deceased, who witnessed the appellant strangulating his mother with the 'saria', as well as the corroborating statements of PW-9, PW-17, and PW-18.
witness_credibility: The court assessed the main witnesses as credible, noting that their depositions inspired confidence and they stood the test of cross-examination.

legal_representation.accused: Shikhil Suri, Shiv Kumar Suri, Advs.
legal_representation.state: Ms. Pinky Anand, ASG, Ashok Panigrahi, P. S. Sudheer, Ms. Kirti Dua, B.V. Balaram Das, Advs.

investigation_status: FIR registered in FIR No.205/2010, charge sheet filed, trial completed

appeal_history.trial_court: Convicted under Section 302 IPC and sentenced to life imprisonment
appeal_history.high_court: Dismissed the criminal appeal, confirmed conviction and sentence
appeal_history.supreme_court: Partly allowed the appeal, modified conviction to Section 304 Part II and imposed 10 years’ simple imprisonment

prosecution_argument: The prosecution argued that the appellant strangulated his wife with a 'saria' and caused her death, and that the incident occurred in a sudden quarrel without premeditation. They relied on the testimony of multiple witnesses, including the son of the victim, to establish the guilt of the appellant under Section 302 IPC.
defence_argument: The defence argued that the incident occurred in a fit of anger and under the influence of liquor, and that the appellant did not intend to kill his wife. They submitted that the case falls under Exception 4 to Section 300 IPC, as the act was committed in a sudden quarrel without premeditation and in a heat of passion.
legal_principle_applied: The Supreme Court applied the legal principle that Exception 4 to Section 300 IPC requires four ingredients: a sudden fight, no premeditation, the act committed in a heat of passion, and the offender not taking undue advantage or acting in a cruel or unusual manner.
precedent_relied_upon: Surinder Kumar v. Union Territory, Chandigarh (1989) 2 SCC 217
sentencing_rationale: The final sentence of 10 years’ simple imprisonment was imposed because the court found that the case fell under Exception 4 to Section 300 IPC, and the act was committed in a sudden quarrel without premeditation, thus modifying the conviction from Section 302 to Section 304 Part II.
